# Jubilees Chapter 24 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 24:5 — "three weeks of years" duration

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Isaac dwelt in Gerar three weeks of years" | Literal Jubilees chronological formula |
| LOGOS | "Isaac dwelt in Gerar for three weeks of years" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "Isaac settled in Gerar for twenty-one years" | Converts to plain number |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Three weeks of years" should be preserved as Jubilees' characteristic chronological idiom — it encodes the book's heptadic time structure. PNEUMA's "twenty-one years" is accurate but strips the theological significance of the formula.

---

## 24:11 — "living water" vs. "spring water"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "living water" | Literal mayim ḥayyim |
| LOGOS | "spring water" | Clarifies the technical term |
| PNEUMA | "spring water" | Same clarification |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. In this context, "spring water" accurately conveys the technical distinction (flowing, fresh water vs. stagnant cistern water). However, "living water" is the traditional biblical phrase with theological resonance in later tradition; the choice is close. Adopted LOGOS for readability.

---

## 24:11-13 — well name treatment

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Contention... Enmity... Spaciousness" | Translations only, no transliteration |
| LOGOS | "Esek — Contention... Sitnah — Enmity... Rehoboth — Spaciousness" | Transliteration + translation |
| PNEUMA | "Esek — Quarrel... Sitnah — Hostility... Rehoboth — Wide Open Space" | Different English glosses |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. Providing both the transliterated Hebrew/Ge'ez name and the English meaning is the standard scholarly approach for place-name etymologies. PNEUMA's "Wide Open Space" and "Quarrel" deviate slightly from the traditional English renderings. EMET's translation-only approach loses the proper names.

---

## 24:20 — "red pottage" vs. "red stew"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "that red pottage" | Traditional KJV rendering |
| LOGOS | "that red stew" | Modern English |
| PNEUMA | "that red stuff — that stew" | Dynamic, Esau's casual speech |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Red stew" is clear and modern. "Pottage" (EMET) is archaic but recognizable. PNEUMA's "that red stuff — that stew" is evocative of Esau's breathless state but inserts words not in the text.

---

## 24:22 — "Esau despised his birthright" — emphasis

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "and Esau despised his birthright" | Literal final note |
| LOGOS | "And Esau despised his birthright" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "He didn't care at all about the birthright he'd just handed over" | Explanatory expansion |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET. The terse biblical formula "Esau despised his birthright" carries its weight precisely because it is brief and unadorned. PNEUMA's expansion ("he didn't care at all") is paraphrase. The formula should be rendered as tersely as the Ge'ez states it.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
